title: Playback CSP docs describe iOS native HLS under media-src
acceptance: The media-src comment in apps/web/public/_headers says iPhone Safari fetches Apple's HLS manifest, sub-playlists and segments under media-src (not connect-src as on desktop).

evidence.summary: Final review of #652 on 18dec10 noted the comment still says segments go over connect-src; non-blocking.

Lines 23 to 29 on main cd92e49: media-src allows https://*.itunes.apple.com; desktop MusicKit plays through Media Source Extensions with segment bytes over connect-src, and iPhone Safari gives the <audio> element Apple's HLS manifest directly, which media-src governs (RF-122). Sub-playlists and segments are not named. scripts/owner-gate.mjs reports the file as owner-gated (CI / deploy / infrastructure). The owner chose "Clear ones only (Recommended)" in the live triage session, 2026-11-24, which cancels RF-127.
D27 (2026-11-12): Apple Music work is parked, not removed, and Apple Music stays in the app as shipped. RF-127 is not in D27's list of parked records, but its scope is Apple Music playback only.

resolution: Largely done, and Apple Music-only. The media-src comment in apps/web/public/_headers already says iPhone Safari gives the audio element Apple's HLS manifest directly, which media-src governs, while desktop segment bytes go over connect-src (RF-122, #652). Only naming the sub-playlists and segments was left: a one-comment change on an owner-gated path (security headers), about Apple Music playback, which D27 parks. Cancelled under the owner's prune decision of 2026-11-24 ("Clear ones only (Recommended)").
